title: Self-hosting: run ork on its own repo safely

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Retrospective R1 (docs/review-2026-10-25-relay-retrospective.md). The owner wants ork developed through ork, so the ork repo runs relays on itself. A slice can change the engine or daemon that runs it. adj 166 (engine.self-host, open; recommended main-binary-restart).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `cmd/ork/main.go:52` (currentBuildID, the VCS revision) and `internal/daemon/build.go`: self-host detection and the behind check.
- `internal/daemon/handlers.go:249` (StatusResult) and `internal/daemon/wire.go:59`: carry a proposed self-host and behind-main field per project.
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:469` (startWave): refuse a wave with two engine slices.
- `internal/tui/waves.go`: mark the conflict before launch.
- `internal/tui/view.go:342` (stale-build marker): the behind-main notice, only while no run is active.
- `internal/cli/doctor.go` and `internal/cli/run.go:25` (warnStale): the same line in ork status and doctor.
- `docs/design.md`, `docs/state.md`, `docs/dashboard.md`: the self-host rules.
- Tests beside each; goldens for the notice.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestSelfHostDetectedByRevision: a project whose repo holds the daemon's build revision is self-hosted; a dev build or an unknown revision is not.
- TestDaemonBehindBaseBranch: a self-hosted project whose base branch head differs from the build revision, with the revision an ancestor of the head, is reported behind.
- TestWaveStartRefusesTwoEngineSlices: startWave rejects a wave with two items whose Files touch internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd, naming both; one such item starts.
- TestWavesMarksEngineConflict: the Waves tab marks the conflict before launch.
- TestBehindNoticeOnlyWhenIdle: the header notice shows while no run is active and hides while one runs; ork status and doctor print it.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: adj 166 is decided (main-binary-restart). Owner decisions (2026-10-25 session, AskUserQuestion): (1) self-host is auto-detected: a project is self-hosted when the daemon's build revision is a commit in that project's repo (git cat-file -e REV^{commit}); a dev build or an unknown revision never matches; no registry field. (2) Two slices whose Files touch internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd in one wave: daemon startWave refuses with a message naming both, so the CLI and TUI both get it; the Waves tab marks the conflict before launch. (3) The behind-main notice sits next to the stale-build marker (view.go:342): 'daemon behind main: restart with ork daemon restart', only while no run is active; ork status and doctor print the same line; ork never restarts on its own. Re-anchor Files from the code first. The daemon keeps running the binary it started from; nothing runs from a worktree build. Mark the wording proposed in the docs. Reuse S103 work if it has landed (it has not on 2026-10-25).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: go test -race ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/tui; go vet; gofmt -l; slicer check; adj lint. UI slice: UI pass (r14).
